about: SI Agent offline answers for Al Ain. Written only from cases/al-ain.json, cases/al-ain.numbers.json and cases/traps.json. 'used' names the number or card each answer comes from.
overview: All four farm circles are Fallow by NISAR's radar rule on 28 Oct: none has a crop echo of +3 dB or more above the desert. But MODIS greenness disagrees for Pivot A, and the HLS photo check hasn't arrived, so the badge is Unchecked (radar only).

qa.a: By the radar rule, all four pivots are Fallow on 28 Oct: none has a crop echo of +3 dB or more above the desert. Pivots C and D have been quiet for years in the MODIS record (last green years 2021 and 2023). Pivots A and B were green this summer.
qa.used: Measured: Pivot A–D · card: Four farm circles, two dates

qa.a: Only time can tell. In 26 years of MODIS greenness, Pivots A and B were green this summer, while C and D have been quiet for years. One quiet season is not the same as a farm left for years.

qa.q: Why does MODIS disagree about Pivot A?
qa.a: Radar says Pivot A is fallow, but MODIS NDVI was 0.67 on 16 Oct. MODIS pixels are 250 m, a third of a circle, so it is our history source, not the formal check. It suggests our 3 dB rule misses some green crops; we don't change a rule after seeing results, so the HLS check will decide.

The badge is Unchecked (radar only). The NASA HLS photo-based NDVI check needs AppEEARS files that haven't been downloaded yet. When they arrive: 75% or more of pivots agreeing = Strong, 50–74% = Moderate, below that = Weak.

North-west of Al Ain, centre-pivot sprinklers make green circles in the desert, each about 800 m across. Some look green, some look bare. The question: which farms went quiet, and is that normal? One picture can't tell you; time can.

As a crop grows, its leaves and stems twist more of the beam into the HV echo, so HV rises; at harvest it falls back. We compare each pivot with a desert control on the same date. A crop counts as present at +3 dB or more above the desert.
qa.used: Lesson: HV follows the growing cycle · method

qa.a: Pivot A's crop echo above the desert was +1.5 dB on 18 Jun, +6.5 dB on 16 Oct and +2.4 dB on 28 Oct. On the latest pass it is below +3 dB, so the class is Fallow. MODIS says it was green this summer (NDVI 0.67 on 16 Oct).
qa.used: Measured: Pivot A · Pivot A pass series

qa.a: Pivot B's crop echo above the desert was +2.2 dB on 18 Jun, −1.3 dB on 16 Oct and +1.2 dB on 28 Oct: Fallow. MODIS calls it green this summer, with NDVI 0.18 on 16 Oct.
qa.used: Measured: Pivot B · Pivot B pass series

qa.a: Pivot C's crop echo above the desert was −0.8 dB on 18 Jun, −1.2 dB on 16 Oct and −0.8 dB on 28 Oct: Fallow. MODIS says it has been quiet for years; its last green year was 2021.
qa.used: Measured: Pivot C · Pivot C pass series

qa.a: Pivot D's crop echo above the desert was −0.4 dB on 18 Jun, −0.8 dB on 16 Oct and −0.4 dB on 28 Oct: Fallow. MODIS says it has been quiet for years; its last green year was 2023.
qa.used: Measured: Pivot D · Pivot D pass series

qa.q: Why are the farm circles blurry on the map?
qa.a: A farm circle is about 800 m across. At NISAR's 10 m science resolution it is clear; on a 280 m map tile, the sharpest NISAR tiles that work, it is a blur of about three pixels (trap 2).
qa.used: Card: The field on a map tile · trap 2

qa.a: No. A simple 'dark = water' rule would call 283.8 km² of this desert 'water'; it's smooth sand. Calm water and dry sand both send the beam away, so both look dark (trap 11).
qa.used: Card: Dark ground next to the farms · trap 11

qa.a: Radar can't say why any farm went quiet, or who decided it. It only shows whether a crop echo is there. Whether a quiet field will be planted again is also beyond what radar can prove.
qa.used: Verdict: what the radar can't prove

qa.a: 3 of 3 passes: 18 Jun, 16 Oct and 28 Oct 2026, NISAR GCOV track 056, ascending. The interference check found no patch over Al Ain on any pass.
